provenance.tag_commit_byte_equality: reported in root retrieval; not independently refetched

decision: Exact source supports a possible cross-read ordinal restart mechanism; saved historical cause remains unproven. Descriptor-specific proof merits a separate minimal source design.
mechanism: fs_locks.c2864-2887: start sets printed li_pos=pos+1, takes file_rwsem write and blocked_lock_lock; stop releases. Mutations use read side of file_rwsem. Ordinary locked iteration is protected; do not claim arbitrary concurrent mutation within one such iteration.

fs_seq_file.c225-293: EOF after positive output returns copied bytes while retaining advanced m->index. EOF is not latched across subsequent read calls. seq_hlist_start_percpu1102-1113 restarts by counting ordinal positions in the current per-CPU lists.

Suppose initial29 visible/unblocked records end with A/B at indices27/28. First raw read returns29 rows and index29. Two persistent insertions before A/B between stop and next start shift A/B to indices29/30. Next read starts29 and labels them30/31, producing suffix28:A,29:B,30:A,31:B while each object still exists only once.

Insertion at a per-CPU hlist head (fs_locks.c602-611) can precede the tail in enumeration. Two net entries before tail suffice; one independent-inode churn child alone has at most one simultaneous flock, so it need not reproduce this mechanism.

PAGE_SIZE does not prevent this scenario: a positive short read at apparent EOF can be followed by another read from TextIOWrapper.read(2MiB+1). It is the gap between raw reads, not a full page requirement. No historical syscall trace or mutation schedule was captured.

model_review.scope: All-visible unblocked short-batch/no-overflow cursor model. New prefix markers model records, not real kernel lock objects. Not general seq_file emulation or historical reproduction.

fdinfo: fs_proc_fd.c23-83 resolves task/fd under task/files locks and get_file pins the selected struct file. show_fd_locks filters fl_file==filp and owner==files or filp under inode flc_lock (fs_locks.c2826-2861). FLOCK creation sets both fl_file and fl_owner=filp (428-437).

A matching fdinfo FLOCK ADVISORY WRITE row describes an actual lock attached to that referenced open file description at observation. Ordinal is local presentation, not a unique lock identity. Normal local flock conflict rules serialize independent descriptions, but syscall dispatch permits filesystem-specific flock implementations.

fdinfo uses single_open: single_next advances index1, single_start then returns NULL (fs_seq_file.c557-585). It does not restart through a growing global ordinal table. Overflow can regenerate a single record before copying; no historical atomicity claim follows.

The temporary file reference can survive target fd closure. Separate PID/start, fd, inode and path checks are not one atomic snapshot; fd reuse and dup/inherited references require controlled lifetime invariants. A row does not prove parent is the only descriptor holder or that no intervening unlock occurred. PID is stored acquisition identity translated through proc namespace, not exclusive descriptor ownership.
Later fdinfo cannot retroactively rescue the failed original global check. Missing/inaccessible/malformed/wrong-inode/wrong-mode evidence must deny new admission.
minimal_next_design: Prepare a new separately reviewed descriptor-proof version; do not edit the original guard or reclassify r3. Bind actual retained parent fd number, owner PID/start/argv, canonical singleton regular lock path and fstat identity. Keep descriptor parent-only and never unlock/close until all owned children drain.

Read bounded complete fresh fdinfo for that exact fd, bracket owner/path/fd identities, require one exact expected FLOCK ADVISORY WRITE whole-file row; missing/conflicting/ambiguous fd evidence denies. Existing acquire/lifetime contract and platform/filesystem assumptions remain necessary.

Retain complete original global listing for diagnosis. Conservative policy may deny missing/conflicting same-inode FLOCK records; accepting repeated target rows only when every field except printed ordinal is identical and exact descriptor proof passes is a deliberate new policy, not deduplicated old-proof success. Inspect same-inode conflicts beyond original expected-owner filter.

No retry-until-success. Conservative global disagreement may still produce false negatives from non-atomic enumeration. Synthetic negative controls and source review precede any runtime use; this report authorizes no lock probe or runtime modification.
